newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - Aug 1.

text.p: Lease inducements tax free, court rules: The Court of Appeal has removed a major uncertainty in tax law, declaring that a massive lump-sum payment from a building owner to induce Coopers & Lybrand partners to move office is tax free. Page 1.
Telecom should sell numbers -- Prebble: Telecom should be required to sell business and individuals their telephone numbers, says Act leader Richard Prebble. Page 1.
Audit poses threat to Kirton's cabinet seat: The audit of an advertising campaign for free healthcare for children threatens Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton's seat in the cabinet. Page 2.

Car crusader says death threat won't stop him: Clocked-car crusader Dermot Nottingham claims there is a contract out on his life as anger builds over his campaign which has already reaped $400,000 from nabbed car dealers. Page 3.
Todd and St John declare their planned 'no' vote: The Todd interim review of New Zealand Superannuation contained few surprises, when the results were announced on Thursday. Page 3.

Ten new laureates for Hall of Fame: Ten present and former business leaders were on Thursday night inducted into the Enterprise New Zealand Trust Business Hall of Fame at a gala dinner in Wellington Town Hall. Page 5.

Picton left to consider future of ferry terminal: Tranz Rail has yet to reveal its hand following the granting of a resource consent to build an inter-island terminal at Clifford Bay as an alternative to Picton. Page 9.
Timber exporters seek lifting of US ban: The New Zealand forest Industries Council has begun a campaign to get US restrictions on New Zealand softwood imports lifted. Page 9.

Body will monitor the act: Complaints from both rural and urban business interests have prompted Environment Minister Simon Upton to set up a Resource Management Act monitoring scheme which $2 million has been set aside for the next three years. Page 10.
Farmers get the burnt chop: Beef prices are on the rise and the exchange rate has tumbled in recent weeks. Page 1.

Winebox commissioner appeals Smellie decision: Winebox commissioner Sir Ron Davison is to appeal last week's ruling by Justice Robert Smellie, ordering the commission to provide wide-ranging discover of some 5,000 winebox inquiry documents. Page 3.
Lion shouts Stella Artois: Lion Breweries is next week expected to counter Dominion Breweries' runaway success with the Netherland's Heineken by importing the Belgian beer, Stella Artois. Page 3.

Council in the gun over 'misleading' Britomart ads: The Audit Office is expected to uphold a complaint next week about the Auckland City Council's allegedly misleading publicity about the controversial Britomart transport centre. Page 4.
Alliance slams ECNZ split: The Alliance is panning government plans to split ECNZ as "blatant empire-building". Page 4.

Qantas loses ground at Lizard Is: New Zealand property investor Don Fletcher and Hong Kong-based SEA Holdings out-manoeuvred Qantas Airlines by leasing the ground under Queensland's exclusive Lizard Island resort from Suncorp for $16 million. Page 6.
Powercos go back to court: Utilicorp NZ will appear in the High Court today seeking an injunction to stop Power New Zealand's independent directors Utilicorp shares held by Power New Zealand. Page 8.
